It also improved and increased communication among clients and their health-care providers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The program has saved money and improved the quality of life of clients , according to research conducted to measure the program&amp;rsquo ; s value . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Nolan thinks the work being done by paramedics in Renfrew contains valuable lessons for the Ontario government , which has vowed to make changes to help relieve an overburdened health system . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We think we have a unique position in the community to solve many of the problems presented as hallway medicine . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;29198;TOOLONG ... hunger : ' Residents in three Ottawa ridings are among highest food bank users in the province&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;29233;TOOLONG ... " data-portal-copyright= " Getty Images " **28;29450;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1347813 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;29480;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; More people are ending up in Ontario emergency rooms because of alcohol use , according to a study headed by Ottawa researchers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Those ER visits are increasing faster among women and young people between the ages of 25 and 29 , according to the study published Monday in the Canadian Medical Association Journal . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;div class= " page " title= " Page 1 " &gt; &lt;div class= " layoutArea " &gt; &lt;div class= " column " &gt; &lt;p&gt;Researchers at the Institute for Clinical Evaluative Sciences , The Ottawa Hospital , the Bruy ? re Research Institute and the University of Ottawa sifted through 2003-2016 hospital administrative data from across the province . In that time , there were more than 765,000 emergency room visits in Ontario attributable to alcohol . The rate of alcohol-related emergency department visits increased 4.4 times more than the rate of overall visits . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The top reason for alcohol-related ER visits was intoxication , accounting for 44.6 per cent of visits , followed by harmful use at 21.4 per cent of visits , withdrawal at 11.4 per cent and alcohol dependence at 10.9 per cent . Alcohol-related ER visits peaked for women around legal drinking age . For men , it was in their early 50s. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/div&gt; &lt;/div&gt; &lt;/div&gt; &lt;p&gt; ER visits are the &amp;ldquo ; tip of the iceberg , &amp;rdquo ; said senior author Dr. Peter Tanuseputro , a researcher , physician and assistant professor at the University of Ottawa . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The bodily harms are often not the biggest issue . It&amp;rsquo ; s the impact on the family . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Men were still at more risk of alcohol-related harm , but women are catching up . Between 2003 and 2016 , alcohol-related ER visits by women ages 25-29&amp;nbsp ; increased by 240 per cent . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Young people are drinking in more harmful patterns , and they&amp;rsquo ; re not aging out of it , said lead researcher Dr. Daniel Myran , a family physician and public health and preventive medicine resident at the University of Ottawa . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There&amp;rsquo ; s a generational effect . Younger women who were drinking in the early 2000s are still drinking more . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The numbers stem from the period before Ontario started to increase the ways people could access booze , which raises questions about Ontario&amp;rsquo ; s new policies around buck-a-beer , tailgating parties and making alcohol available in more locations for longer hours . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Increasing prices for alcoholic beverages through taxation or price minimums have been proven to be effective policies to reduce alcohol consumption , particularly for younger drinkers and heavy drinkers , said Dr. Sheryl Spithoff , a family and addiction medicine physician at Toronto&amp;rsquo ; s &lt;br&gt; Women&amp;rsquo ; s College Hospital . Government retail outlets and limiting hours of operation and outlet density are measures that have been endorsed by the World Health Organization . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The Ontario government has gone in the opposite direction with such glee and without any embarrassment , &amp;rdquo ; said Timothy Stockwell , director of the Canadian Institute for Substance Use Research at the University of Victoria . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He points out that there are peaks and troughs in alcohol consumption that appear to coincide with economic factors . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There was falling alcohol consumption around the time of the financial crisis . But about the time of the recovery , people started to drink again , &amp;rdquo ; Stockwell said . &amp;ldquo ; In the past five years , there has been a rapid uptick in deaths and hospital presentations . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The study is just one piece of evidence in a growing pile that suggests alcohol has grave costs . Among other illnesses , alcohol causes liver disease , addiction and withdrawal problems , heart damage and cancer . Cancer Care Ontario estimates that 3,000 cancer diagnoses a year could be spared in the province if people followed safe alcohol consumption guidelines . Between two and seven per cent of breast cancer cases can be attributed to alcohol consumption . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There is also a massive cost to the healthcare system . Costs attributable to alcohol were $4.32 billion Canada-wide in 2014 , according to the Canadian Centre on Substance Use and Addiction and the Canadian Institute for Substance Use Research . Alcohol-related deaths increased by 26 per cent for women and by five per cent for men between 2001 and 2017 , according to the Canadian Institute for Health Information . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Despite the alarming statistics , there is still a lot of public ignorance about the relationship between alcohol and serious illness . According to one survey reported by Cancer Care Ontario , only one-third of Canadians are aware that they can lower their cancer risk by reducing their alcohol consumption . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Prohibition is not the answer , Spithoff said . But she urges governments to ban all promotion of alcohol use , including marketing , branding and events sponsorships . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At the very least , governments should consider applying the rules it uses for tobacco promotion to alcohol . Alcohol is at least as harmful as tobacco and shouldn&amp;rsquo ; t be treated differently , she said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Tobacco kills more people . But having an alcohol addiction is more likely to result in disruption to people&amp;rsquo ; s lives . If you include harms to others , alcohol is the most harmful substance out there , &amp;rdquo ; Spithoff said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; re not saying that alcohol shouldn&amp;rsquo ; t be available , but that it should be available in a public health model . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Spithoff points to a framework introduced in Scotland which set national prevention goals . An awareness campaign introduced this spring called &amp;ldquo ; Count 14&amp;rdquo ; was developed to demonstrate what 14 alcohol units actually means and encourages Scots to think about how their weekly drinking adds up . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In Canada , the guidelines for low-risk consumption are not more than two drinks a day , 10 in a week , or three drinks on a special occasion for women . For men , it&amp;rsquo ; s three drinks a day , 15 in a week , or four on a special occasion , according to the National Alcohol Strategy Advisory Committee at the Canadian Centre on Substance Use and Addiction . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And a &amp;ldquo ; serving&amp;rdquo ; of alcohol is actually rather small . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A standard 750 ml bottle of wine contains more than five servings and a serving of beer is 341 ml . To compare , a pint of beer is 568 ml &amp;mdash ; so two pints a day is over a man&amp;rsquo ; s daily limit . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Our study shows that people aren&amp;rsquo ; t meeting those guidelines . They&amp;rsquo ; re not even close , &amp;rdquo ; Tanuseputro said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Is a glass of wine a day still considered good for health ? Not according to a &lt;a href= " https : **33;29516;TOOLONG ... published last year i&lt;/a&gt; n the British medical journal The Lancet , based on analysis of data from 195 countries and territories , which concluded that even one drink a day increases health risks . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The widely held view of the health benefits of alcohol needs revising , particularly as improved methods and analyses continue to show how much alcohol use contributes to global death and disability , &amp;rdquo ; the study concluded . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Our results show that the safest level of drinking is none . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The emergency room study wasn&amp;rsquo ; t designed to reveal the causes behind by increases in certain groups . But Myran suggests marketing alcohol to women has become increasingly targeted and sophisticated . It&amp;rsquo ; s treated as a female empowerment issue . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It can be very seductive . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Reducing alcohol consumption takes a concerted effort on the part of people who are concerned about public health and safety , said Stockwell of the Institute for Substance Use Research . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s pretty low down on the agenda politically . You have people in one area collecting revenue and other people who are aware , but who don&amp;rsquo ; t have the power . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Stockwell is one of the researchers involved in a Health Canada-funded project introduced in the Yukon last November . Colourful warning labels were placed on alcohol bottles and cans . One label warned consumers that alcohol can cause cancer . Another outlined the recommended maximum number of drinks per day . Four weeks after the launch , the Yukon Liquor Corp . halted the research in response to concerns from the alcohol industry . The study is going ahead , but the cancer label has been dropped and replaced with one about standard drink sizes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What will it take to shift consumption levels in any meaningful way ? A calamity and some high-profile champions , said Stockwell . People think of alcohol they way they think about food and the role it plays in celebrations and bringing people together . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We are all blissfully unaware that this does so much harm , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a silent problem . We don&amp;rsquo ; t question it much . It&amp;rsquo ; s like the industry owns parts of our minds . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **33;29551;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; " data-portal-copyright= " Errol McGihon " **28;29899;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1425114 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;29929;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Could Ottawa become Canada 's -- or even the world 's -- healthiest city ? In an occasional summer series starting today , Brigitte Pellerin explores what it would take . &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ask the people around you what a healthy city looks like . Chances are their answer will be something like : A healthy city is one where most of the people eat well , exercise a bunch and live long lives free of chronic disease . And that&amp;rsquo ; s probably true . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But what if we have it backwards ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What if a healthy city is one that makes people **25;29965;TOOLONG to be healthier ? A town , a community , that inspires its citizens naturally to make the kinds of healthy lifestyle choices that endless nagging fails to do ? What if it&amp;rsquo ; s the environment &amp;mdash ; which includes the people we surround ourselves with &amp;mdash ; that makes us healthier , not the other way around ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And what if Ottawa could be the healthiest city of them all ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;29992;TOOLONG ... title= " Jake Cole of the Sierra Club Canada Foundation , left , and columnist Brigitte Pellerin enjoy the pedestrian pathways in Ottawa . " alt= " Jake Cole of the Sierra Club Canada Foundation , left , and columnist Brigitte Pellerin enjoy the pedestrian pathways in Ottawa . " data-portal-copyright= " Errol McGihon " **28;30028;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1425114 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; According to the most recent &lt;a href= " http : **34;30058;TOOLONG ... of Ottawa 's Health&lt;/a&gt; report by Ottawa Public Health , 67 per cent of us think our health is either very good or excellent , which is more than the average in the rest of Ontario ( henceforth affectionately dubbed the ROO ) , at 61 per cent . But one-third of Ottawa adults are overweight while 23 per cent are obese , which is similar to rates in the ROO. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On the other hand , our life expectancy at birth , at 81.9 years for men and 85.2 years for women , compares favourably to ROO numbers ( 80.5 and 84.5 years , respectively ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So we&amp;rsquo ; re pretty good . But we can be better . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For starters &amp;ndash ; &amp;nbsp ; and it&amp;rsquo ; s no surprise &amp;ndash ; Ottawa Public Health thinks we should eat more veggies and move about more . More than one-third of Ottawa adults don&amp;rsquo ; t meet the exercise guideline of 150 minutes a week ; 59 per cent of youth spend more than two hours a day sucking a screen ; and nearly half our kids fail to get eight hours of sleep at night . Not a recipe for living to a ripe old age . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It is estimated that fully 70 per cent of premature deaths ( that&amp;rsquo ; s what we call dying before the age of 75 ) can be avoided by preventing the onset of disease or by delaying the progression of disease with proper detection and treatment . We have doctors and hospitals for the second part . It&amp;rsquo ; s the first one , prevention , that you and I could work on more . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; How ? Maybe what we need is to become something of a &amp;ldquo ; Blue Zone . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This has nothing to do with political parties ( whew ! ) . Rather , it&amp;rsquo ; s &lt;a href= " https : **33;30094;TOOLONG ... a book&lt;/a&gt; of the same name by Dan Buettner , identifying five areas in the world where people live long , healthy lives , and where spry centenarians are more common than elsewhere : Okinawa , Japan ; Sardinia , Italy ; Nicoya , Costa Rica ; Ikaria , Greece ; and Loma Linda , California . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;30129;TOOLONG ... title= " The beachfront in the village of Therma , on Ikaria , Greece . Ikaria is considered one of the healthiest places on Earth . Ottawa is n't Greece , but we have lots of advantages that could make us all healthier . " alt= " The beachfront in the village of Therma , on Ikaria , Greece . Ikaria is considered one of the healthiest places on Earth . Ottawa is n't Greece , but we have lots of advantages that could make us all healthier . " data-portal-copyright= " Howard Fagen " **28;30165;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1425112 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Buettner identified nine principles that contribute to making Blue Zones the healthiest areas to live in : &amp;ldquo ; move naturally&amp;rdquo ; ; &amp;ldquo ; purpose&amp;rdquo ; ; &amp;ldquo ; down shift&amp;rdquo ; ( i.e. reduce stress ) ; &amp;ldquo ; 80 per cent rule&amp;rdquo ; ( stop eating before you&amp;rsquo ; re full ) ; &amp;ldquo ; plant slant&amp;rdquo ; ( eat less meat ) ; &amp;ldquo ; wine @ 5&amp;rdquo ; ( moderate drinking ) ; &amp;ldquo ; belong&amp;rdquo ; ( faith/community ) ; &amp;ldquo ; loved ones first&amp;rdquo ; ( family ) ; and &amp;ldquo ; right tribe&amp;rdquo ; ( social network ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Blue Zones project , inspired by the book , aims to help cities apply those nine health principles to their own environment , as a way to help citizens become healthier . And it appears to work . Fort Worth , Texas , decided to try turning blue a few years ago . It went from nearly dead-last in the Gallup-Sharecare Well-Being index of American cities in 2014 , to 58th out of 185 in 2017. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;30195;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s the kind of progress that makes people pay attention &amp;ndash ; including in the Calgary suburb of Airdrie , which aims to become the first Canadian city certified as a Blue Zone . Airdrie &amp;amp ; Area Health Cooperative&amp;rsquo ; s Stacey Lush said the certification is a few years out , but &amp;ldquo ; Airdrie is ready to put the boots to the pavement and work hard to get healthy . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ottawa : If that&amp;rsquo ; s not a challenge , I don&amp;rsquo ; t know what is. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What would we need to make our city &amp;ldquo ; bluer&amp;rdquo ; &amp;ndash ; or at any rate healthier ? Could we apply some of the Blue Zones principles to help us lead happier , healthier lives ? What would that look like ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Grab your carrot sticks and sensible shoes and we&amp;rsquo ; ll take a stroll in the fresh air over the next few weeks , as we discuss how to make our region as healthy as it can be . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **32;30231;TOOLONG Pellerin&lt;/strong&gt; is an Ottawa writer who wants this city to be the healthiest in Canada . Her occasional series will appear on Tuesdays and Fridays . &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;30265;TOOLONG ... " data-portal-copyright= " Julie Oliver " **28;30488;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1406167 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Anxiety levels are high among some physicians at The Ottawa Hospital as it transitions to a new electronic health record system . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One doctor , who contacted this newspaper , said some physicians feel they were not adequately trained before the June 1 launch and are not receiving the support they need . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We feel abandoned . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a statement , the hospital&amp;rsquo ; s director of communications and engagement , Kate Eggins , said that 98 per cent of physicians had training . Additional training and support were also provided . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We take concerns of staff and physicians seriously and we encourage them to speak openly to colleagues and management when they have a concern . we have always acknowledged that moving from a paper system to a digital one would require substantial change to workflows , processes and procedures . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The doctor also said the number of glitches in the system is much higher than physicians had expected and will take months , not weeks , to correct . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I am shocked by the amount of glitches . The system is in relative chaos right now . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Ottawa Hospital is one of six Eastern Ontario health organizations to adopt the Epic electronic health record system . Several other Ontario hospitals , including CHEO , had previously adopted the U.S.-developed system that is used around the world . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Dr. Alan Karovitch , an internal medicine doctor who is vice-president of the medical staff association at The Ottawa Hospital , agreed that the transition has been stressful. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; People have to understand this is the biggest process change any of us will see in our careers . Change management is hard . But if you keep your eye on the prize and contextualize it , you realize this is OK. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;30518;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;30560;TOOLONG ... woman 's appendix bursts during lengthy wait to be admitted to **29;30595;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;30626;TOOLONG ... record system brings some delays , frustrations at The Ottawa **29;30661;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; Karovitch said he has been well supported throughout the process and , although there have been frustrating days , he has always felt supported , confident about patient care and that things are improving . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I think it is good for patient care &amp;mdash ; no more sticky notes on charts , no more faxes . We are getting out of that . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The doctor who spoke to this newspaper and a second physician said that they are concerned about potential errors and delays during the glitch-prone rollout of the Epic system , as well as expanding wait lists for appointments and non-urgent surgery . The doctor said he had issued eight &amp;ldquo ; tickets&amp;rdquo ; to report issues with the system and has not even received an acknowledgment about when they will be fixed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This newspaper has been told that 10,000 tickets &amp;mdash ; representing issues with the system &amp;mdash ; were filed within the first two days after its launch . He agreed to speak on the condition of anonymity , saying he feared for his job . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The transition is adding significantly to physicians&amp;rsquo ; workloads , the doctor said , tripling the amount of work being done in some cases . That means they are spending more time looking at computers than with patients and is slowing things down . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In some cases it has led to delays in transferring patients from one campus to another . It is also increasing the risk of errors in scheduling tests and medication . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The irony is that so many things don&amp;rsquo ; t work , we have the worst of both worlds . We still have to fax things , &amp;rdquo ; said the doctor . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Another physician said the new system has resulted in chaos and low morale and set the stage for dangerous situations . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Duplicate bookings , the physician said , are common . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A woman who was taken to the General campus by ambulance on June 2 , the day after Epic launched , experienced that . She said she was on her way to having a second , unnecessary , CT scan before she questioned why and health workers discovered it was an error . This newspaper has heard other reports of duplicate tests being done . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The hospital has added extra staff to help with the transition and has brought in superusers to help in the early weeks . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One of those super users , Bassil Abuzeid , a recent Carleton University economics graduate who was trained to help support staff learning the new system , said he understands the transition is difficult . &amp;ldquo ; But from the superuser point of view , the system is not as bad as people think . It is meant to be more convenient for the staff . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Abuzeid said that in his experience staff members were catching on to the new system quickly . The result will be an improved information flow , he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I think the system creates transparency between the departments and is much more convenient . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The move to fully digitalize health records has been slow in Canada , with doctors offices and hospitals relying on faxes and handwritten notes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Eggins , said some transition slowdowns were anticipated and the hospital has taken steps to minimize them . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She also said a fully digital health records system is necessary . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The era of the fax machine has to go . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The doctor said physicians were given a chance to test the system and familiarize themselves with it ahead of time , but there were so many problems with that &amp;ldquo ; play space&amp;rdquo ; that they got little practice , which has left them feeling unprepared . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Under the new system , doctors and nurses are responsible for many of the tasks previously done by others &amp;mdash ; including scheduling and ordering medication . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Some positions will been cut as a result , although the hospital says it will retrain people whose positions are made redundant . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The doctor conceded that some things are improving but said it feels like the complex new system has been rolled out too quickly and with too little support for those using it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The situation is discouraging and stressful for many physicians , who feel they are spending more time with the computer than with sick patients . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We are really dedicated and invested in good patient care . " data-portal-copyright= " DAVID TALUKDAR " **28;31393;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1408778 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;The start of menstruation is a sign of reproductive health and nature 's rite of passage from childhood to womanhood . It has a huge influence on a girl 's sense of identity and self-worth . However , in the developing world , where adequate sanitation facilities ( separate latrines for girls and boys , for example ) are rare , menstruation can be a barrier to education , employment , equity , empowerment and a sense of self-worth. &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Unfortunately in too many cultures , it is also a taboo subject shrouded in shame and secrecy . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;In fact , UNICEF data show that one-third of schools in the developing world do not even have adequate facilities . In sub-Saharan Africa , this figure is nearly 50 per cent . This can open girls up to ridicule , taunting or even sexual harassment . In an attempt to find the only privacy available to attend to their needs and clean themselves up , some wait until darkness to go in the woods , where they risk being sexually assaulted or attacked . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;There is also an issue of silence . Most girls have very little information about what is happening to their bodies . According to WASH United , one girl in three in South Asia knew nothing about menstruation before the onset of her first period . Many more have only a vague idea of what they are supposed to do during menstruation . In Sri Lanka , one study found that only 41 per cent of girls had good overall knowledge of menstrual health management . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;More commonly , girls will simply refuse to go to school during menstruation . If they miss five days of school a month ( 25 per cent ) , they can fall further and further behind until the situation can seem hopeless and they drop out . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Girls who drop out of school tend to have lower earning potential , more menial jobs , be married off earlier and be subjected to more frequent partner violence . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Even for the lucky ones who stay in school and get jobs , they may still have to deal with inadequate facilities for their menstruation needs . This can translate into absenteeism , lack of promotion opportunities and ultimately , forgone income . For those who start their own businesses , the problem is compounded by having to leave their business unattended several times a day , in an attempt to find the few private spots available to attend to their needs . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;If you consider all the days a woman menstruates in her lifetime , it amounts to years . Embarrassed or ostracized , she may cut herself off from school , work , social interaction and being a full participant in her community . This is like serving a sentence of years of house arrest . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Most important is to understand that in failing to resolve this situation , we are all paying a price . It is high time this situation received priority attention . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Women Deliver is the world 's largest gathering on the health , rights and well-being of women and girls . Canada hosted the global conference in Vancouver recently . At the conference , the prime minister announced the government will invest $14 billion over 10 years to promote the health and rights of women and girls around the world . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;A smart investment for some of this money would be to help equip all schools and workplaces with basic separate sanitation facilities and culturally appropriate hygiene products . Elizabeth Payne , Jon WillingWed , 24 Apr 2019 21:19:04 **45;32564;TOOLONG ... &amp;amp ; ChildLocal NewsMenPoliticsWomenThe drug resistant fungus that is putting health officials on alerthttp : **35;32611;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;32648;TOOLONG ... title= " File photo . " alt= " File photo . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;32684;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1059346 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; A Winnipeg resident returned from India seriously ill with a brain abscess and a chronic ear infection . The unidentified patient , who had undergone dental surgery in India , was infected with a drug-resistant form of bacteria . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And that was not all . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The 64-year-old is now recognized as Canada&amp;rsquo ; s Patient Zero for an emerging new threat that has hospitals across the country on alert &amp;mdash ; multi-drug resistant Candida auris . The fungal infection was found in the patient&amp;rsquo ; s ear when &amp;ldquo ; cheesy&amp;rdquo ; fluid was drained from it and tested . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Candida auris can spread from patient to patient and can live on skin , walls , curtains , handles , cellphones and other surfaces . The risk of infection in otherwise healthy patients is relatively low ; Candida auris can colonize the skin of patients with no visible impact . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But in people with suppressed immune systems , it can cause a serious infection , enter their bloodstream and even be deadly . In some countries where it is common , mortality rates for those with invasive Candida auris are higher than 50 per cent . What is more , treatment options are limited or non-existent , and it is difficult to eradicate . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And that is worrisome to hospitals , because many have significant populations of patients with suppressed immune systems &amp;mdash ; those undergoing cancer treatment or transplant patients , for example . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;32714;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;32756;TOOLONG ... technology sanitizes smart phones in hospitals with UV **26;32791;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; What has health officials most concerned about Candida auris is how difficult it is to identify , treat and contain &amp;mdash ; especially its persistence . A recent New York Times story described a hospital having to rip out floor and ceiling tiles in order to eradicate it from an infected patient&amp;rsquo ; s room . It can also live on reusable medical equipment . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I think it is something that all hospitals are worried about , &amp;rdquo ; said Dr. Julianne Kus , a clinical microbiologist at Public Health Ontario . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Canada has seen only 19 cases of Candida auris . Those cases include a cluster in British Columbia and five unrelated cases in southern Ontario . None of the Ontario cases was multi-drug resistant . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The authors of the paper about Patient Zero , who was diagnosed in May 2017 , note that multi-drug resistant Candida auris was first identified in Japan in 2009 and has , since then , become an emerging global threat . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The fact that it behaves differently than other infectious threats &amp;mdash ; even clinging to synthetic surfaces and forming a biofilm &amp;mdash ; makes it so hard to eradicate . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Humans are colonized with many strains of Candida , notes Kus . Sometimes , they can cause infections such as vaginal yeast infections and athlete&amp;rsquo ; s foot that are more a nuisance than serious infections . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What makes Candida auris different , though , is that it can be spread from person to person , similar to bacteria and viruses . &amp;ldquo ; Typically , we have never really been concerned about fungi or yeast spreading from person to person , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What is more , Candida auris appears to be able to spread from a person into the environment and back to a person . When the strain is multi-drug resistant and resistant to disinfectant cleaning products , it quickly can become a nightmare for hospitals . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It seems to be acting a little bit differently . We haven&amp;rsquo ; t really thought about fungi this way before , &amp;rdquo ; said Kus. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Another complicating factor is that treatment for fungal infections is limited and anti-fungal drugs can be harmful so must be used judiciously . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Earlier this year , Public Health Ontario published a document guiding health officials in the province on how to approach the emerging health threat . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Among other advice : Rooms of patients or residents colonized with C. auris should be cleaned and disinfected daily , or even twice a day and medical equipment used on the patient should not be used on anyone else . C. auris can spread between patients as quickly as four hours and patients can even catch it from being in a room previously occupied by a patient . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The verdict is still out on the impact of ultraviolet light and other disinfectant procedures . There is some evidence that hydrogen peroxide vapour and ultraviolet light can reduce levels of environmental contamination with C. auris , but whether this will result in reduced transmission has not been confirmed , said Kus. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Facilities that are using ultraviolet light or hydrogen peroxide vapour should prioritize rooms housing C. auris patients for the disinfection , but the room should first be cleaned and disinfected using standard procedures , she said , which includes the use of bleach . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There have been no cases in Ottawa , but hospitals are prepared for cases . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Kus says it is important to draw attention to multi-disease resistant infections such as Candida auris. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It highlights that we are still vulnerable to infectious disease . We will not be able to rely on antibiotics forever . &amp;rdquo ; Kus noted that the World Health Organization has named drug resistance as a leading health threat . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Should ( Canadians ) be worried ? In Canada we are doing a pretty good job so far in containing it . We haven&amp;rsquo ; t had the same experience as is happening in the States . I would say from the community level , I would not worry about it . But it is a good thing to talk about . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **27;32819;TOOLONG " **34;32848;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;32884;TOOLONG ... dog kills wild turkey downtown&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " http : **34;32919;TOOLONG ... erupts as LeBlanc sentenced to 15 years for second-degree murder&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;32955;TOOLONG ... The illnesses they cause vary from minor infections to severe diseases . Common strains include C. difficile and MRSA. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; MRSA complications are sometimes as minor as small skin infections or as serious as pneumonia . Similarly , C. difficile can result in symptoms ranging from diarrhea to life-threatening inflammation of the colon . Both bacteria can live for weeks on hard surfaces , such as cellphones or tablets . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; By harnessing a specific wavelength of ultra-violet light that is refracted in the chamber of the device , CleanSlate UV attacks bacteria on mobile phones and other electronic devices so that it can no longer reproduce . The process takes 20 seconds &amp;ndash ; allowing time to use the hand-sanitizer located conveniently next to it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There have been numerous studies that show that one in four mobile hospital devices will have a pathogen bacteria on it , &amp;rdquo ; said Taylor Mann , co-founder of CleanSlate UV. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This is a growing concern , as the number of mobile devices used in hospitals is steadily increasing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Hospitals put a huge focus on hand hygiene , &amp;rdquo ; Mann explained . &amp;ldquo ; But it doesn&amp;rsquo ; t make sense to wash your hands and then immediately touch a dirty device . Hospitals are deploying these very expensive touch-screen products to make their routine easier . &amp;rdquo ; Sanitizing the mobile devices is often not thought of until after they are purchased . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;33176;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;33218;TOOLONG ... drug resistant fungus that is putting health officials on **26;33253;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; The CleanSlate UV provides a non-chemical way of killing bacteria . By putting small identification tags on hospital devices , the CleanSlate automatically records which devices are cleaned and when . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It all adds up to them having more information so that they can protect their staff and patients , &amp;rdquo ; Mann said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Mann expects that the tagging technology will be available to purchase sometime this summer . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;33281;TOOLONG ... flood of 2019 : ' Severe flood levels ' now expected&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;33316;TOOLONG ... Obama is coming to speak in Ottawa&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; Erica EndemannWed , 24 Apr 2019 11:40:03 **45;33386;TOOLONG ... &amp;amp ; ChildLocal **26;33433;TOOLONG policies in Canada and beyond : What 's working and what needs to changehttp : **34;33461;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;33497;TOOLONG ... title= " Dr. Zachary Kaminsky , the chair of suicide prevention , poses for a photo at the Royal in Ottawa Tuesday Feb 6 , 2018. " alt= " Dr. Zachary Kaminsky , the chair of suicide prevention , poses for a photo at the Royal in Ottawa Tuesday Feb 6 , 2018. " data-portal-copyright= " Tony Caldwell " **28;33533;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1382531 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Between 70 and 80 people take their own lives in Ottawa every year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Dr. Simon Hatcher , a psychiatrist and researcher in clinical epidemiology at The Ottawa Hospital Research Institute , said he believes it&amp;rsquo ; s possible to reduce that number by 20 per cent within five years . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s been done before . It&amp;rsquo ; s not rocket science , &amp;rdquo ; he says , pointing to the example of the Nuremberg model , a protocol first used in Germany which has now spread all over Europe and beyond . &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m sure it can be reduced . We can do better . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Suicide is considered a public health issue . But Ottawa Public Health has not set a target for reducing suicide in the city . Even the issue of setting targets is controversial . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m not sure setting a target will help . What will help is setting a collaborative approach , &amp;rdquo ; said Ben Leikin , supervisor of Ottawa Public Health&amp;rsquo ; s mental health team and co-chair of Suicide Prevention Ottawa , which recently merged with the Ottawa Suicide Prevention Coalition . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s also important to consider whether a reduction in the number of suicide deaths and attempts would continue over time . There are some environmental factors , such as natural disasters or large-scale layoffs for example , that can&amp;rsquo ; t be controlled and have an effect on the suicide rate , says Leikin. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Leikin said while he applauds those who have set a target for suicide reduction , Ottawa has not . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Any evidence that exists out there , we&amp;rsquo ; re open to it . Let&amp;rsquo ; s not reinvent the wheel . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There have been a number of strategies touted to prevent suicide . Here are a few of them . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;33563;TOOLONG ... title= " Psychologist Dr. Antoon Leenaars. " alt= " Psychologist Dr. Antoon Leenaars. " data-portal-copyright= " Jean Levac " **28;33599;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1382530 " /&gt; **28;33629;TOOLONG **33;33659;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;What is it ? &lt;/strong&gt; This &amp;ldquo ; continuous improvement model , &amp;rdquo ; first implemented in health-care systems in the U.S. , works on the idea that people who have contact with the health-care system can be prevented from taking their own lives . There are three main pillars : a direct approach to suicidal behaviours , continual improvement of the quality and safety of care processes and an organizational commitment to the aspirational goal of zero suicides. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Among the measures : removing the lethal means of suicide ; training a competent and caring workforce ; using screening to determine who is at risk of suicide ; ensuring all patients at risk are closely followed ; treating suicidal ideation independent of the patient&amp;rsquo ; s diagnosis and transitioning patients with &amp;ldquo ; warm hand-offs and supportive contact . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Does it work ? &lt;/strong&gt; The Henry Ford Health System , a non-profit health-care provider in the Detroit area that includes eight hospitals , 48 medical centres and 13 walk-in clinics , has often been named as an example of good outcomes . Henry Ford , which calls the protocol &amp;ldquo ; perfect depression care , &amp;rdquo ; introduced it in 2001 . In a study published in 2007 , Henry Ford reported a 75 per cent reduction in the suicide rate . There were actually zero suicides in the Henry Ford system for an 18-month stretch between 2009-2010. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The model has moved into Europe and Canada . The first Zero Suicide campaign in Canada was unveiled in May 2016 at the St. Joseph&amp;rsquo ; s Healthcare Foundation in London , Ont. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The model is not without controversy in the mental health community . Hatcher says there is one major problem with translating the zero suicide model : three-quarters of people who die by suicide have no contact with mental health services in the year leading to their death . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There&amp;rsquo ; s a lot of rhetoric about it , but not a lot of evidence , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &amp;ldquo ; It irritated a lot of clinicians by calling it Zero Suicide . It&amp;rsquo ; s like going into intensive care and saying , &amp;lsquo ; There will be zero deaths . &amp;rsquo ; As a psychiatrist , I am responsible for getting ( my patients ) the best treatment possible . The implication here is that we are responsible for a death by suicide . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Zero Suicide works for hospitals and health-care networks , not for regions and jurisdictions , said Leikin. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There is also debate over whether zero is an attainable goal . Zero Suicide calls it an &amp;ldquo ; aspirational challenge and practical framework for system-wide transformation . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I think we should shoot for Zero Suicide . But it will never happen . There will always be people with unbearable angst . Our task is to work toward it , &amp;rdquo ; says psychologist Dr. Antoon Leenaars , the former president of the Canadian Association for Suicide Prevention . &lt;/p&gt; **27;33694;TOOLONG Nuremberg **31;33723;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;What is it ? &lt;/strong&gt; The Nuremberg Alliance Against Depression was initiated in 2001 as a community-based model project in the German city of Nuremberg , which has about 500,000 residents . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;How does it work ? &lt;/strong&gt; Called a &amp;ldquo ; multi-level intervention , &amp;rdquo ; it&amp;rsquo ; s a four-level approach that engages partners from parents to police officers to family physicians . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; First level : General practitioners and pediatricians are invited to educational workshops on how to recognize and treat depression in the primary care setting . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Second level : An awareness campaign for the general public is aimed at improving knowledge and reducing stigma . Campaigns have included posters , advertising spots in movie theatres , brochures , public events and websites . Local organizers are also urged to develop a relationship with the media to prompt discussion , and to set guidelines on coverage to prevent copycat suicides. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Third level : Patients in high risk groups &amp;mdash ; such as teens in crisis &amp;mdash ; are given &amp;ldquo ; emergency cards&amp;rdquo ; guaranteeing direct access to professional help . Local self-help groups are provided with expert advice and partnerships are created with patient associations . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Fourth level : Workshops are held with groups such as health-care professionals , counsellors , clergy and police officers . There are also information sessions for parents , teachers and youth workers and prevention programs in schools . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The program also tracks data on &amp;ldquo ; core indicators&amp;rdquo ; such as number of suicides , number of suicide attempts , public opinion , attitudes , knowledge and media coverage of suicides. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Does it work ? &lt;/strong&gt; A lot of other jurisdictions have adopted it . After suicidal behaviour was reduced by 20 per cent in Nuremberg , 18 partners in 17 European countries established the &lt;a href= " http : //www.eaad.net/ " &gt;European Alliance Against Depression&lt;/a&gt; in 2004 . There are now about 100 regional networks in the alliance . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Mental Health Commission of Canada&amp;rsquo ; s &lt;a href= " https : **33;33756;TOOLONG ... of Hope&lt;/a&gt; suicide prevention program , which has been adopted by communities in Labrador , Newfoundland and New Brunswick , has some parallels , but the European Alliance has stricter protocols . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;33791;TOOLONG ... title= " NDP MP Charlie Angus stands in the House of Commons during question period on Parliament Hill in Ottawa on June 9 , 2015. " alt= " NDP MP Charlie Angus stands in the House of Commons during question period on Parliament Hill in Ottawa on June 9 , 2015. " data-portal-copyright= " FRED CHARTRAND " **28;33827;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 794461 " /&gt; &lt;div class= " mceTemp " &gt;&lt;/div&gt; **25;33857;TOOLONG national **34;33884;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;What is it ? &lt;/strong&gt; More than 20 countries have a national strategy for suicide prevention . Canada has a federal framework , but not a strategy , and that needs to change , argues the Centre for Suicide Prevention , a branch of the Canadian Mental Health Association . The Canadian Association for Suicide Prevention has also been calling for a national strategy for more than 20 years and &lt;a href= " https : **31;33920;TOOLONG " &; ... a blueprint&lt;/a&gt; in 2004 and an update in 2009. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Canada is the only G8 country without a national suicide prevention strategy and one of the few industrialized countries that doesn&amp;rsquo ; t have one , according to the Centre for Suicide Prevention . The U.S. , Australia , Japan , Scotland , England and Finland all have working national policies in place . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The centre says research shows that a strategy must address suicide directly and have its own prevention strategy , outside the broad umbrella of mental health , &amp;ldquo ; otherwise there is a danger that the prevention message will be diluted , ignored , or lost altogether . &amp;rdquo ; The strategy also can&amp;rsquo ; t be the responsibility of a single government department , but must be addressed by all government departments and sectors affected , including the community , workplace , schools , families , the criminal justice system and education . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Does it work ? &lt;/strong&gt; Finland was one of the first countries to introduce a national strategy in the 1980s , and the suicide rate there dropped by nine per cent over 10 years , according to the Centre for Suicide Prevention . Scotland introduced a strategy in 2002 and saw an 18 per cent reduction in suicides by 2012. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Jackie Doyle-Price was named the United Kingdom&amp;rsquo ; s first Suicide Prevention Minister in October 2018 . Her role oversees a strategy that includes a focus on how social media and technology , such as predictive analytics and artificial intelligence , can help identify suicide risk . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; England&amp;rsquo ; s strategy was introduced in 2012 . In a progress report published in January , Doyle-Price said the suicide rate in England was at its lowest in seven years . &amp;ldquo ; However , these rates can change over time , &amp;rdquo ; she noted . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Achieving a low rate and maintaining it over time is an eternal problem in suicide prevention . In the U.S. , which has a national strategy , the suicide rate increased 24 per cent between 1999 and 2014 , from 10.5 to 13 suicides for every 100,000 people . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; NDP MP Charlie Angus introduced a parliamentary motion for a national suicide prevention &amp;ldquo ; action plan&amp;rdquo ; earlier this year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We need to put language to this that says this is an epidemic , that it&amp;rsquo ; s causing devastation , &amp;rdquo ; says Angus. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It also has to be a made-in-Canada plan that recognizes the realities of vulnerable groups in Canadian society , such as Indigenous Peoples , and the relationship between the provinces and federal government when it comes to health policy , he says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Among other measures , &lt;a href= " https : **32;33953;TOOLONG ... motion , M-174&lt;/a&gt; , calls for a national public health monitoring program , national standards of training for those who work with vulnerable populations and an annual report to Parliament , which would include data on progress for the previous year . &amp;ldquo ; If we&amp;rsquo ; re not diminishing the numbers of deaths , then the plan is not working , &amp;rdquo ; said Angus. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The motion is up for second debate on May 2 . If it passes , Angus said Canada would be obligated to put a number of steps in place , including identifying groups at elevated risk and introducing strategies that would prevent suicide among these groups within 18 months . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I was shocked at the level of suicide among middle-aged men , &amp;rdquo ; said Angus. &amp;ldquo ; When a large industrial plant goes down , we need to have a plan to raise awareness ( about suicide ) . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; **37;33987;TOOLONG the biology of **43;34026;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;What is it ? &lt;/strong&gt; Scientists are delving into the complicated interplay between genetics and environment and the role each plays in suicide risk . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For example , molecular biologist Zachary Kaminsky&amp;rsquo ; s research hit the news in 2014 after he and colleagues at Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore discovered a chemical alteration in a gene called SKA2 linked to stress reduction . The finding suggested that doctors could identify suicide risk and even prevent suicide through a blood or saliva test . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But it&amp;rsquo ; s complicated , said Kaminsky , who is now the DIFD Mach-Gaensslen Chair in Suicide Prevention Research at The Royal&amp;rsquo ; s Institute of Mental Health Research . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Kaminsky did a study of about 925 soldiers deployed to Afghanistan . A blood test identified a variant of SKA2 , correctly identifying five soldiers who had elevated scores for suicidal ideation. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But the tests also found a high number of false positives &amp;mdash ; these soldiers tested positive , but they did not have suicidal thoughts . That brings up the question of identifying people who are not at risk . There&amp;rsquo ; s also the problem of identifying those who are at risk , but not being able to do anything to help them . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We have to understand if we will cause a problem that we have no solution for , &amp;rdquo ; said Kaminsky. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Does it work ? &lt;/strong&gt; Researchers are learning more and more about the interplay for genetics and the environment . But it&amp;rsquo ; s not as simple as administering a once-in-a-lifetime blood test to everyone to determine whether or not an individual is genetically vulnerable to suicidal thoughts . First of all , genes may be switched on or off by traumatic or stressful events . Biological systems are adaptive to experiences . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s not just genes . It&amp;rsquo ; s context , &amp;rdquo ; said Kaminsky. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At the same time , vulnerability to suicide risk is believed to be determined by a complex interplay of genetic factors . &amp;ldquo ; Is there one gene that does it all ? If I said that , I would get ripped apart , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; In term of coming up with a magic bullet that works for everyone , it becomes very challenging . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But he also has a lot of hope . At some point , a negative test result may conclude that someone is not at risk of suicide , for example . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The more research we do , the more we understand about the biological systems that will lead to more treatment targets , &amp;rdquo ; said Kaminsky. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Treatments target systems we believe to be dysregulated with the hope of bringing them back in line . The more we know , the more we will be able to do this correctly . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He uses an analogy : A car owner notices the coolant is low , so he adds more . Then it runs low again , so he adds more . Adding more solved the problem for a time , but not the underlying problem . The mechanic figures out that the problem is the water pump . &amp;ldquo ; Once fixed , no more symptoms and no more treating the symptoms because the treatment was better . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There are also promising new drug treatments for helping people in crisis . In March , the FDA approved a new depression treatment in the form of ketamine , which has been used as a painkiller , anesthetic and recreational drug , delivered as a nasal spray . A study of depressed patients at imminent risk of suicide in emergency rooms at 11 centres in the U.S. found the treatment resulted in significantly rapid improvement in depressive symptoms &amp;mdash ; including some measures of suicidal ideation. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt; &lt;strong&gt;FEATURE STORY&lt;/strong&gt; : &lt;a href= " https : **33;34071;TOOLONG ...
