" data-portal-copyright= " Tony Caldwell " **28;34250;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1382524 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;34280;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Lauren Richards died on Feb. 21 by suicide . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;The incident , outlined in cryptic terms by authorities , made the news because Richards died in a public place . We could tell you where and how , but the Canadian Psychiatric Association in its guidelines for journalists cautions against reporting on the details . Suicide contagion is real . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Richards ' name has never been released . But her family and friends say there is a story behind the few bare paragraphs in a press release , a tale of unbearable mental anguish and a question that still haunts them : what could be done to stop someone from dying when death is what they desire so fervently and seek so avidly ? &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; About 11 people die by suicide every day in Canada , according to the Canadian Association for Suicide Prevention . On average , another 200 Canadians attempt suicide every day . This is likely an underestimate . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Based on data from the Canadian Community Health Survey , 14.7 per cent of Canadians have thought about suicide and 3.5 per cent have attempted suicide in their lifetime . Suicide is ranked as the ninth leading cause of death in Canada , but the second leading cause of death , after accidents , for young people between the ages of 15 and 34. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It is a public health conundrum that has never been solved . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;34316;TOOLONG ... title= " Jennifer Richards and her son Simon pose with a photo of Lauren Richards in Ottawa Wednesday March 27 , 2019 . Lauren died Feb. 21. " alt= " Jennifer Richards and her son Simon pose with a photo of Lauren Richards in Ottawa Wednesday March 27 , 2019 . Lauren died Feb. 21. " data-portal-copyright= " Tony Caldwell " **28;34352;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1382524 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; About 6,000 people go the emergency rooms of the General and Civic campuses of The Ottawa Hospital every year seeking help for a mental health crisis . About half of these report having suicidal thoughts , says Dr. Simon Hatcher , a researcher at The Ottawa Hospital Research Institute . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Richards was 26 years old when she died and had been struggling with mental health issues since high school , say her friends and family . She had bulimia as a teen and attempted to take her own life many times . She swallowed pills and cut herself so often that she started to wear long sleeves all the time in her late teens . On at least two occasions , she needed stitches . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Only 12 days before her death , Richards posted a photo of herself on Instagram , pale and propped up by pillows . She is smiling faintly . The photo clearly shows the scars of self-inflicted wounds that line her upper arms . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t it be great if we could talk about our mental health/illnesses or show our scars without judgment from others ? &amp;rdquo ; reads her post . &amp;ldquo ; If you have mental health problems , don&amp;rsquo ; t be afraid to talk about them . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Richards was in unbearable mental pain . When her brother Simon heard that a woman had perished on the news , he immediately thought of his sister . There was a flurry of texts . Before long , 11 people were waiting at a friend&amp;rsquo ; s house , dreading the arrival of the police . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I had a strong fear of getting a phone call like this . It was like my worst fears had been realized . It was the worst thing I could imagine , &amp;rdquo ; says Simon . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;34382;TOOLONG ... title= " Lauren Richards took her own life on Feb. 21 , 2019 . She was 26. " alt= " Lauren Richards took her own life on Feb. 21 , 2019 . She was 26. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;34418;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1382528 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In 2017 , after Richards was discharged from hospital after yet another round of treatments , she was diagnosed with depression and possibly borderline personality disorder , although she did not meet the criteria for a formal diagnosis . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Borderline personality disorder , known as BPD , is a condition characterized by fraught relationships , impulsiveness , extreme emotions and , sometimes , recurrent suicidal behaviour . Its hallmark is instability : an unsteady sense of self and emotions . People with BPD sometimes also suffer from depression , eating disorders and substance abuse . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To have BPD is to be on a constant roller coaster of emotions . Patients are often dismissed as needy , drama queens and attention-seekers , even by health professionals . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Going to lose my mind , not because I have BPD , but because of all the stigma attached to it . PLEASE educate yourself before you judge me : ) &amp;rdquo ; Richards posted on Instagram a month before her death . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Even though BPD affects only one to two per cent of the population , between five and 10 per cent of people who have the illness die by suicide . Most suicides are found in two major diagnoses : depression and BPD , says Dr. Antoon Leenaars , a Windsor-based psychologist and suicide researcher who is the former president of the Canadian Association for Suicide Prevention . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; They are constant fodder in the news because their behaviour is both perplexing and sometimes deadly to themselves . An inquest into the suicide death of Carleton University student Jason Simon heard in January that an emergency room psychiatrist suspected Simon had BPD . It was one of several diagnoses given to Justin St. Amour , whose suicide inquest heard earlier this month that he had planned to strip naked and freeze to death in a cemetery &amp;ldquo ; because I have more in common with the dead than the living . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; People with borderline have a very fragile existence . Often they have volatile relationships , with impulsivity and a fear of real or imagined abandonment . They are difficult patients . They have very difficult lives , &amp;rdquo ; says Leenaars. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; They create chaos . It&amp;rsquo ; s hard for them not to . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Yet patients describe the emotional pain they feel as real &amp;mdash ; and intolerable . The American suicidologist Edwin Shneidman called it &amp;ldquo ; psychache. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Suicide cries to the mind as a solution because life is constantly breaking into a thousand pieces , &amp;rdquo ; says Leenaars. &amp;ldquo ; They are always skating on thin ice . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;34448;TOOLONG ... title= " Artwork by Lauren Richards . " alt= " Artwork by Lauren Richards . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;34484;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1382522 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Richards may have been struggling , but she was also a resilient young woman with plans for her life , say her family and friends . She was a talented artist . Her favourite subjects were elderly and weather-beaten people , their faces intricately creased with lines and wrinkles . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; She was fun , easy to love , &amp;rdquo ; says Karen Wallace , who met Richards when she was in middle school . Richards became a friend to her daughter , Margot . &amp;ldquo ; We immediately loved her . She was open , fun-loving , a kind person . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The first hints of mental illness appeared in Richards&amp;rsquo ; teen years . She became increasingly withdrawn , and seemed to prefer spending time in her room . She spent two years at Algonquin College and friends believe the self-harm got worse then . She started wearing long sleeves all the time to cover her scars. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the past decade , Richards has been treated in almost every hospital in Ottawa . Around 2011 , she started seeing her family doctor about low moods and bulimia. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It was the hard part for any parent . One day , she would seem happy . If you saw her , you wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t have got the idea that she was a depressed person , &amp;rdquo ; says her mother , Jennifer Richards . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After she graduated in 2012 , Richards embarked on a degree in social work at Carleton University . She overdosed on Tylenol in December 2013 and was admitted to the General campus of The Ottawa Hospital . She later told her friends there had been previous suicide attempts , but she had kept them private . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In 2014 , Richards began to see a psychiatrist and took part in an outpatient program for eating disorders . She continued to struggle with depression , but found the structure of university helpful and graduated from Carleton with distinction in 2015. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In May 2016 , Richards overdosed and was admitted to intensive care at the Montfort Hospital . She was discharged two days afterwards without a referral for mental health support , say her friends . A couple of days later , she admitted herself to the General campus because she was still experiencing suicidal thoughts . She stayed there for about three weeks then transferred to The Royal and was released around June 2016. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the fall of 2016 , Richards had an overdose and spent months at The Royal . She had another episode in November 2016 , which sent her to the ICU at the General campus for about a week and was then sent back to the Royal . She started electroconvulsive therapy while at The Royal , which affected her memory . She was prescribed medications and took lithium injections. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;ALSO : &lt;a href= " https : **33;34514;TOOLONG ... policies in Canada and beyond : What 's working and what needs to change&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Brooke Clark met Richards while they were both at The Royal . Being admitted to hospital was like winning a lottery , says Clark . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; People don&amp;rsquo ; t want to deal with it . Psychiatrists don&amp;rsquo ; t want to deal with it . It&amp;rsquo ; s like a revolving door . Being rejected is like a slap in the face , &amp;rdquo ; she says . &amp;ldquo ; We talked about the revolving door . We talked about the fact that they would stop admitting borderline people after a while . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Richards was discharged from The Royal in February 2017 . Dialectic behaviour therapy &amp;mdash ; known as DBT , the psychotherapy that those in the mental health field have called the &amp;ldquo ; gold standard&amp;rdquo ; for treating BPD &amp;mdash ; was what she needed to get better . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The waiting list for DBT was months long . She began the program in September 2017. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; DBT takes about a year . It uses mindfulness training &amp;mdash ; how to accept and live in the moment &amp;mdash ; and teaches patients how to cope in a crisis , manage distressing emotions without trying to escape , ask for what they need and say no when they must . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; One of the things to do is to accept the unacceptable . This is what you have to do , &amp;rdquo ; says Leenaars. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; DBT seemed to be the glue that was holding things together . &amp;ldquo ; She was able to pull all of those skills out of the toolbox , &amp;rdquo ; says mother Jennifer . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I felt she was almost there . I was hoping it was true . You think your daughter is getting better . Then the disease just takes over . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Richards struggled with the fear of knowing that the DBT program would end . She felt she had no stability and feared abandonment . Two weeks before the program ended , she stopped showing up because she was upset it was ending . To try to ease her transition , the DBT psychiatrist said Richards could choose between herself and the community psychiatrist . This decision was too difficult for her to make , said her friends . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;34549;TOOLONG ... title= " Lauren Richards took her own life on Feb. 21 , 2019 . Just weeks before , she had posted on Instagram about mental health . " alt= " Lauren Richards took her own life on Feb. 21 , 2019 . Just weeks before , she had posted on Instagram about mental health . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;34585;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1382525 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Richards&amp;rsquo ; friends and family believe there must be something that could have made a difference . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We have to start thinking outside of the box . We could all have used a course , &amp;rdquo ; says Karen Wallace . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; If someone has cancer , we don&amp;rsquo ; t turn them away from the door of the hospital . There&amp;rsquo ; s something out there . We have to figure out how to tap into it . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Jennifer says there was not enough professional support for Richards and the people who were close to her . Jennifer found dealing with her daughter&amp;rsquo ; s mental illness to be isolating and at times overwhelming . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I believe that our health-care system must place more emphasis on suicide prevention , to give more support and direction not only to those individuals who are suffering , but also to their loved ones . I was not made aware of any support group for loved ones , &amp;rdquo ; she says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Despite visiting Lauren daily for long periods of time while she was in the hospital , we received little information and guidance . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Health professionals could do more to educate and support the families of patients and include them in safety or action plans that could result in greatly improved outcomes for patients at risk , she says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Obviously , patient confidentiality is important , but common sense and judgement don&amp;rsquo ; t seem to factor in as they should in the case of suicidal individuals . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There would be no question that a patient whose kidneys have failed needs dialysis , but the same is not true of patients with mental health conditions , says Leenaars . Help is not available , or there&amp;rsquo ; s a long waiting list . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Suicide is a public health epidemic . But very little is being done . Hospitals in the 90s had more services available than there are now . It&amp;rsquo ; s all bare bones now , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I don&amp;rsquo ; t have a solution , &amp;rdquo ; says Margot Wallace . &amp;ldquo ; But if these populations are so vulnerable , why do they have to advocate for themselves ? I think there has to be a better way to do this . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;34615;TOOLONG ... title= " Rachelle Bourget ( R ) and Margot Wallace were friends of Lauren Richards , who died by suicide on February 21 . April 10 , 2019. " alt= " Rachelle Bourget ( R ) and Margot Wallace were friends of Lauren Richards , who died by suicide on February 21 . April 10 , 2019. " data-portal-copyright= " Errol McGihon " **28;34651;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1382523 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It is the sad truth that between five and 10 per cent of people with BPD die by suicide , says Dr. Joel Paris , a psychiatrist , expert in BPD and professor emeritus at McGill University , where he was chair of the department of psychiatry between 1997 and 2007. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The scientific question is whether we know enough to predict and prevent such events . Unfortunately we don&amp;rsquo ; t . And that is why I have suggested working with suicidal patients in outpatient therapy rather than hospitalizing them . Most experts on BPD agree with me on this point . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Guilt is one of the most common reactions of families and friends to a suicide . That and wondering what else they could have done . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; This is understandable , but fails to take into account that some patients have such a strong wish to die that they come to believe this is the only way to relieve their pain , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; And we don&amp;rsquo ; t know whether we could reduce the suicide rate with a better mental health system . Suicide prevention remains a hope rather than a proven thing . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s tricky to draw firm conclusions about whether there has been any success in preventing suicide among BPD patients . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; One can not compare different studies to show that we are succeeding in preventing suicide in BPD . I would like to believe that this is the case , given all the effort we have put into helping clinicians and their families identify this disorder , &amp;rdquo ; says Paris . &amp;ldquo ; But I see no way to prove it . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Youth suicide in Canada has gone down in recent decades , for example , says Paris . &amp;ldquo ; But we really have no idea why . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Organizing safety networks of supportive friends and family probably does good . But Paris , again , has seen no research showing they make a difference in death by suicide . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We do not have good data on how many BPD patients in Canada die by suicide . Again , you can not generalize from following a clinical sample , and we have no population data , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There have been studies in the past in Montreal using psychological autopsy &amp;mdash ; in-depth family interviews after death &amp;mdash ; which suggest that about 30 per cent of youth suicides have BPD. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; But the majority of these cases were men . Most of our patients are women , and it is well known that men are more likely to die by suicide , while women are more likely to make multiple attempts , &amp;rdquo ; Paris says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; ******** &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Richards belonged to a close-knit circle of friends and they refused to give up on her . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Giving up on Lauren wasn&amp;rsquo ; t an option , ever , &amp;rdquo ; says her friend Rachelle Bourget. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Her friends created a safety net and were in constant contact . They smuggled her family&amp;rsquo ; s dog Buster into The Royal in a backpack during one long-term stay . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Lauren was a charmer . We would go up to her room at The Royal and the nurse would be braiding her hair , &amp;rdquo ; says Bourget. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Richards didn&amp;rsquo ; t have the typical profile of a BPD patient . She didn&amp;rsquo ; t abuse drugs or alcohol or become embroiled in turbulent , high-drama relationships . She had ambition , embarking on an online master&amp;rsquo ; s degree while holding down two jobs . She adopted a rescue greyhound , who she named Winston . It seemed to be a signal that she wanted something to tether herself to life . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; She fought for the life she wanted , &amp;rdquo ; says Bourget. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Much of what Richards&amp;rsquo ; friends and family know about the trajectory of her illness they have had to piece together through what she was willing to reveal . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; This whole idea that we have created a ( society ) where there is no stigma is not true , &amp;rdquo ; says Karen Wallace . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In 2018 , Richards started to research &amp;ldquo ; more lethal&amp;rdquo ; ways to die . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; She called the psychiatrist who she saw on a weekly basis while in the DBT program to say that she wanted to kill herself , &amp;rdquo ; says mother Jennifer . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The DBT psychiatrist stayed on the phone with Richards while also calling for the police to pick her up . &amp;ldquo ; We don&amp;rsquo ; t think this incident resulted in a hospital admission ; we believe that she was brought to see psychiatry and later that night discharged directly from the emergency room . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; According to her friends , there were many more times Richards either brought herself to the emergency room or called police to come get her . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;34681;TOOLONG ... title= " Lauren Richards took her own life on Feb. 21 , 2019 . She was 26. " alt= " Lauren Richards took her own life on Feb. 21 , 2019 . She was 26. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;34717;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1382526 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; In December , Richards self-harmed to the point of needing stitches . No follow up with mental health was ordered . She was sent home , says Jennifer . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Richards was working in a coffee shop , and early this year , she started a second job . She was also taking an online graduate diploma program in mental health and addictions through Dalhousie University . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When it came to her own mental health , she was sometimes desperate . In mid-January , she spent a few nights in the emergency psychiatric ward because she was feeling suicidal , but was not admitted , says Jennifer . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; She would leave to go to work for the next day , then come back . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Richards cut herself on Jan. 22 and was admitted to surgery , where she received stitches . According to her friends , she did not see a social worker or mental health worker . She was admitted to the hospital again on Jan. 30 . She was sent home and , as far as her friends knew , had not been counselled to change anything she was doing . Her friends could see that she was not doing well . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She was also assigned a new mental health worker on Feb. 13 . Mental health workers changed often and Richards came to think of this as another revolving door . She relied on the emergency department because community supports were not enough , say her friends . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; She had to re-tell her story every time , &amp;rdquo ; says Bourget. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; ******** &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Suicide is not inevitable for people with BPD . Some move on to live happy lives . Sometimes , on the other side , they&amp;rsquo ; re incredulous of how intensely they had once wanted to die . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Dr. Joel Paris said he doesn&amp;rsquo ; t know how to predict who will change , or when , but these changes are common . Patients get better for several reasons . People are all a little less impulsive after 30 , possibly because of brain maturation , he said . People learn to avoid situations that are difficult for them . And patients who benefit from therapy learn to apply more effective skills . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Our group in Montreal has shown that the vast majority of patients we treated over the past 15 years went on the recovery , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &amp;ldquo ; BPD is a disorder that usually gets better with time and responds positively to well-designed psychotherapy. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a bombshell 2011 interview , Dr. Marsha Linehan , the pioneering psychologist who developed dialectical behaviour therapy , revealed that she herself had borderline personality disorder . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Linehan was hospitalized in 1961 , at the age of 17 . She had burned her wrists with cigarettes , slashed her arms , legs and midsection with sharp objects , she told The New York Times . When there were none of these in her locked seclusion room , she banged her head against the wall and the floor . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I felt totally empty , like the Tin Man ; I had no way to communicate what was going on , no way to understand it , &amp;rdquo ; she told the Times . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Linehan was a devout Catholic . Things changed for her after she had what she described as a &amp;ldquo ; shimmering&amp;rdquo ; religious vision . She felt she loved herself . A year later , after a relationship ended , she still felt devastated , but didn&amp;rsquo ; t feel she had to harm herself . Linehan went on to get a PhD in 1971 and set about trying to understand what had changed . She called the concept &amp;ldquo ; radical acceptance&amp;rdquo ; &amp;mdash ; accepting yourself as you are . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;34747;TOOLONG ... title= " Lauren Richards with her rescue greyhound , Winston . Richards took her own life on Feb. 21 , 2019. " alt= " Lauren Richards with her rescue greyhound , Winston . Richards took her own life on Feb. 21 , 2019. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;34783;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1382527 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Kate , a 38-year-old Ottawa woman , also came out the other side . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Kate , who asked that her last name not be used , had anorexia and tried to take her life through overdoses on multiple occasions between her teens and early 30s . She was eventually diagnosed with BPD and Bipolar II , which has less elevated &amp;ldquo ; highs&amp;rdquo ; than bipolar disorder . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She wanted to die , and her family did not doubt it . &amp;ldquo ; It feels like you&amp;rsquo ; re drowning with no help . My parents were resigned to the fact that I would die . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; During one of Kate&amp;rsquo ; s hospital stays , she recalls a doctor telling her mother : &amp;ldquo ; How can you stand having her as a daughter ? &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That stung . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; People who feel mental pain are not treated like those who have physical health problems , she says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; How would you treat someone with cancer or a broken limb ? Would you just send them home ? This was very serious . It was a life-or-death experience . I wasn&amp;rsquo ; t looking for attention . I really wanted to die . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When Kate was 32 , things changed all at once . She can&amp;rsquo ; t say for certain what prompted the change , but credits a supportive doctor , being treated with hormones and antidepressants as well as the DBT strategies she had learned . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; My doctor didn&amp;rsquo ; t shame me or embarrass me . She tried to understand . She said the way I felt things was beautiful . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Perhaps it was coincidence , but it was like turning on a light , says Kate . &amp;ldquo ; My depression literally stopped . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She still feels anxiety and uses the strategies she learned in DBT . Now , it&amp;rsquo ; s scary for her to think she was once so determined to die . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There&amp;rsquo ; s nothing I want more than to live . Part of my recovery is to be thankful for the small things &amp;mdash ; the flowers outside , my cat on my lap , &amp;rdquo ; she says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; When you have gone through something that dark , you evolve . I know so much more about myself . I know exactly what I want and what I don&amp;rsquo ; t . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;35064;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 440329 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; If five pedestrians died at a busy crosswalk in a 72-hour period , or five people died in a week from toxic lettuce , the clocks would stop , as the poets say , the authorities would cluster , everything menial set aside . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;But five sons or fathers or mothers who die from drug overdoses in three or four days are , pretty much , a statistic , a sad tally of self-infliction . Maybe five more will die next week , for all we know , for all we 're doing differently today . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; ( And , indeed , it was in London , Ont. &amp;mdash ; not Ottawa &amp;mdash ; where five more men have just died in a six-day period , all of suspected overdoses , prompting the police chief to make a public appeal. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The cluster of overdoses that struck Ottawa in late March has frighteningly occurred across North America . That it appears to involve mixing a fentanyl-type drug into &amp;ldquo ; regular&amp;rdquo ; cocaine is the most alarming aspect , as it exposes a whole population of occasional users to deadly possibilities . The demise of a promising musician and a middle-aged HVAC operator attest to the scary , new territory . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The experts tell us these are users who would not normally have on hand naloxone , the opioid overdose antidote . And the reason is simple : typically , fentanyl , the synthetic opioid that can slow elephants , is added to boost other opioids , like heroin or other morphine-based drugs . Cocaine , meanwhile , is not an opioid , but is being targeted just the same . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; " It is our belief that most of the illicit drug market right now is tainted with fentanyl , " says Andrew Hendriks , Ottawa Public Health 's director of health protection and a leader on an overdose prevention task force . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;35094;TOOLONG ... title= " Andrew Hendriks , director of health protection at Ottawa Public Health . " alt= " Andrew Hendriks , director of health protection at Ottawa Public Health . " data-portal-copyright= " Jean Levac " **28;35130;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1372132 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; It is unclear at this point exactly which drugs killed the five individuals in late March , but history is a tour guide to the most likely scenario in which dozens of local residents overdosed in a matter of hours &amp;mdash ; &amp;ldquo ; complete mayhem&amp;rdquo ; in the words of an experienced street worker downtown . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the summer of 2016 , in a four-day period in July , there was a dramatic increase in the number of overdose patients who arrived in the emergency department at Surrey Memorial Hospital outside Vancouver &amp;mdash ; 43 in all , mostly men . Because of the rapid use of naloxone , 35 patients were treated and soon released , but three ended up in intensive care . One died . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Due to the extraordinary nature of the event , health authorities took the time to do the toxicology . The conclusion was that there was likely a single dealer responsible for distributing crack cocaine spiked with furanyl-fentanyl , a so-called &amp;ldquo ; analog&amp;rdquo ; not seen in Surrey before . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; This is the first reported cluster of overdose events caused by crack cocaine contaminated with furanyl-fentanyl in North American , &amp;rdquo ; says a report submitted to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It would not be the last . Late one night in September of that same year , nine young people in Delta , B.C. , scored some cocaine . In the course of roughly 20 minutes , all nine of them overdosed and needed paramedic or hospital attention for respiratory distress . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Why ? The cocaine was laced with fentanyl or its cousins and the casual users were not habituated to opiate use , which sounds eerily like Ottawa in March 2019 . ( Briefly put , cocaine is an &amp;ldquo ; up&amp;rdquo ; and opioids are a &amp;ldquo ; down , &amp;rdquo ; to the point the respiratory system can stop. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;In June 2018 , about 20 people in Philadelphia -- regular cocaine users from a corner of the city -- were taken to hospital with overdoses in what one physician described as the first coke-fentanyl wave to strike the city . Two of the users died . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While Ottawa police have declined to discuss what might have been at play last week &amp;mdash ; was it a single source , for instance ? &amp;mdash ; we do know something about the illicit drugs being consumed in the city . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The supervised injection site at the Sandy Hill Community Health Centre has used a mass spectrometer to test drugs for up to 18 substances before they are used . The process is voluntary and only takes a couple of minutes . In December , of six cocaine samples , one contained fentanyl , two others had another opioid . In November , of eight samples , four had fentanyl or similar drugs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s amazing how quickly the drug supply proliferated with all these different kinds of cocktails , &amp;rdquo ; said program director Rob Boyd , with fentanyl showing up in a sizable portion of the &amp;ldquo ; stimulant stream . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;35160;TOOLONG ... title= " Rob Boyd , the head of the Oasis harm-reduction program at the Sandy Hill Community Health Centre . " alt= " Rob Boyd , the head of the Oasis harm-reduction program at the Sandy Hill Community Health Centre . " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;35196;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1372134 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The next step is to gather data on the amount of each drug in the mixture , he added , urging safe practices among those using cocaine , even occasionally . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Dr. Dan Ciccarone is a physician and researcher at the University of California in San Francisco . He&amp;rsquo ; s looked at many overdose waves that have struck across North America and spoken to many drug dealers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; These clusters make everyone in the public health world scratch their heads , &amp;rdquo ; he said Wednesday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; His best explanation is that accidental contamination is the likely culprit &amp;mdash ; in shipping and packaging &amp;mdash ; not purposeful mixing of an &amp;ldquo ; up&amp;rdquo ; drug ( cocaine ) , with a &amp;ldquo ; down&amp;rdquo ; ( synthetic opioid ) , even though fentanyl is relatively cheap and easy to ship and mix . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; On the first level , you have to ask why ( mix ) . I have to tell you there&amp;rsquo ; s no good answer . &amp;rdquo ; Fentanyl and its analogs are showing up in just about everything , including meth , he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; All drug streams now all of a sudden have a new level of paranoia in them . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When asked about the stigma of drug use , Ciccarone said the mysterious death of race horses in California is getting more media coverage than the &amp;ldquo ; historic&amp;rdquo ; opioid crisis . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It is so big in the United States that it&amp;rsquo ; s driving the mortality rate up . And yet it&amp;rsquo ; s not being hailed at that level of crisis . I think that&amp;rsquo ; s because of stigma and fear , &amp;rdquo ; he said , then pointing to the slow public health response to the AIDS crisis of the 1980s. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s taking a long time to develop a response to fentanyl because we&amp;rsquo ; re afraid of it . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;BY THE NUMBERS : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 56&amp;nbsp ; Times so-called &amp;lsquo ; purple&amp;rsquo ; samples ( sold as heroin , &amp;lsquo ; down&amp;rsquo ; , or fentanyl ) contained fentanyl and its derivatives from Sept to Dec , at the Sandy Hill safe injection site . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 50&amp;nbsp ; Percentage of cocaine samples that contained a synthetic opioid in November , December , in limited Sandy Hill tests . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 14&amp;nbsp ; Hours between six overdoses attended by paramedics on the same day , including three fatalities . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 40 , 5 : &amp;nbsp ; Emergency departments visits , deaths , from opioid-related causes in June 2018 , Ottawa area . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; $80,000/$1.6 million : &amp;nbsp ; Cost of one kilogram of cut fentanyl , eventual profit from same kilogram , according to the New York Times . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; $0 or $1 : Cost of an ( antidote ) naloxone kit at many pharmacies and of limited-use fentanyl test strip . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To contact Kelly Egan , please call 613-726-5896 or email &lt;a href= " **26;35226;TOOLONG " **33;35254;TOOLONG . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **27;35289;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;35318;TOOLONG ... Dow says medical personnel examining a patient with a possible concussion or head injury often start out by asking that individual if they can move their fingers or hands or having them count backwards , but they don&amp;rsquo ; t think to tell that person to avoid driving for a few days . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Medical personnel &amp;ldquo ; tend to forget&amp;rdquo ; that driving is an everyday activity , particularly for Canadians who don&amp;rsquo ; t live in major city centres , he adds . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To counter that situation , SAAQ has a workshop for physicians and other health personnel to underline the importance of driving and how it should be considered when they&amp;rsquo ; re talking about the impact of whatever has happened on a patient&amp;rsquo ; s life . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To be fair , Hoshizaki says , evaluating incapacity after a concussion is difficult even for specialists , so imagine the dilemma of a layperson trying to figure out if he or she is ready to return behind the wheel . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Physicians can provide guidance , Hoshizaki adds , but there&amp;rsquo ; s no real way of telling people they can&amp;rsquo ; t drive . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; When we talk about guidelines to return to play or ( other ) guidelines , they&amp;rsquo ; re guidelines , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &amp;ldquo ; They&amp;rsquo ; re not rules . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Dow says the process of removing a driver&amp;rsquo ; s licence takes about six weeks , so , effectively , SAAQ tells Quebec physicians to report conditions only if the consequence of previous injury or disease &amp;mdash ; formally called &amp;ldquo ; sequelae&amp;rdquo ; &amp;mdash ; last six months or more . As one example , he refers to a former municipal transit driver who , following a severe concussion , functioned at the cognitive level of an eight-year-old . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Temporary&amp;rdquo ; conditions such as concussions do not have to be reported to provincial authorities unless they affect driving and a patient says he&amp;rsquo ; ll drive anyway . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The point is , if you were advised by your physician not to drive and you do drive and you kill somebody , you can be liable for accidental homicide , which is something you have to bear in mind , &amp;rdquo ; Dow says . &amp;ldquo ; You&amp;rsquo ; re also going to have that on your conscience for the rest of your life . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Looking for **25;36114;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It would be easier to advise someone not to return behind the wheel after a concussion based on specific medical indicators or &amp;ldquo ; biomarkers , &amp;rdquo ; but nobody has figured that out , despite what Hoshizaki describes as &amp;ldquo ; a fair bit of money&amp;rdquo ; invested in research in Canada . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There are known biomarkers for brain injury , Marshall adds , but , because brain injury is a spectrum , even those biomarkers are not useful enough in diagnosing concussion. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Similarly , magnetic resonance imaging ( MRI ) or diffusion tensor imaging ( DTI ) scans can reveal signs of concussion , but Marshall says that again they are neither sensitive nor specific enough to be gold-standard tests for diagnosing concussions . In other words , they could miss diagnosing concussions at the individual level , which is a clinical diagnosis anyway . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The ideal , Schmidt says , would be to use current clinical tools to predict or find patient patterns differentiating between someone who shouldn&amp;rsquo ; t drive and someone who could . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Even though they both have a concussion , maybe you&amp;rsquo ; re having issues with reaction time , and we know that is a better predictor , better indicator of your driving safety , &amp;rdquo ; she says . &amp;ldquo ; However , you&amp;rsquo ; re having more issues with your memory , which might not be as related to your safety in driving . It might hurt your ability to navigate in driving , but you&amp;rsquo ; re OK , your safety on the road is fine &amp;hellip ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; My second preference , then , if that&amp;rsquo ; s not possible because it&amp;rsquo ; s possible that the clinical tools we use now don&amp;rsquo ; t predict those things very well or are not sensitive enough to those things that they wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t work in that way , would be then to introduce a new tool or assessment battery that was short and succinct , but got at someone&amp;rsquo ; s readiness to return to driving so that , clinically , we could return them to driving as soon , as quickly , but as safely as possible . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;36141;TOOLONG ... title= " Dr. Shawn Marshall . " alt= " Dr. Shawn Marshall . " data-portal-copyright= " PROVIDED " **28;36177;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1377388 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Out of the dark&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Guidelines to concussion management have changed , with &amp;ldquo ; return to activity as tolerated&amp;rdquo ; as a general counsel . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Marshall says &amp;ldquo ; return to sport , &amp;rdquo ; is easy since concussed athletes simply must go through established protocols and show themselves to be symptom-free because they&amp;rsquo ; re otherwise at increased risk of injury . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Return to school&amp;rdquo ; is hard , he says , because it&amp;rsquo ; s a distracting environment requiring cognitive and social energy , so &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;a concussed student might have to start off by avoiding&lt;/span&gt; gym or taking only one class . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For driving , perhaps a 10-minute commute would be OK , but not a long vacation trip , says Marshall , who likens it to recovery from a sprained ankle : If you can walk without pain , proceed , but , if walking causes pain , back off temporarily before trying again . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Obviously , if the person is acutely confused and doesn&amp;rsquo ; t know the date or doesn&amp;rsquo ; t know where they are , they shouldn&amp;rsquo ; t be driving . What I didn&amp;rsquo ; t expect was the pain &amp;ndash ; a lot of pain . The heavy bleeding . The weakness , the fainting . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I didn&amp;rsquo ; t know how these things went , so I ended up in the emergency . Instead of rest and a cup of tea , my pregnancy ended with the holy trifecta women know all too well : harsh lights , cold instruments , technical talk . Because the &amp;ldquo ; products of conception&amp;rdquo ; had passed , I didn&amp;rsquo ; t need to undergo a &amp;ldquo ; dilation and curettage , &amp;rdquo ; which is exactly what it sounds like : the uterus is opened up and whatever is left is scraped out . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The nurse cautiously told me about a support group . Somewhere between &lt;a href= " https : **33;37013;TOOLONG ... and 25 per cent&lt;/a&gt; of pregnancies end this way , on average . It&amp;rsquo ; s actually a really tough job to sew these bits of different DNA together in a coherent and functional way . Because of this , miscarriage , well , just happens . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So , why is no one talking about it ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Most women , of course , have heard that early gestation is a somewhat insecure affair . But a large part of the problem lies in the everyday erasement of women&amp;rsquo ; s lived experiences , especially their bodily ones , even more so when these have to do with fertility and motherhood . As any woman will tell you , speaking about the way your own body functions is a complicated and delicate matter that makes almost everyone ill at ease . Most women included . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When I started talking about my miscarriage , a surprising number of women confided in secretive tones that they , too , had silently suffered through pregnancy loss . Many had never told anyone but their partners . Some lost friends who weren&amp;rsquo ; t able to deal with their pain . Grief , after all , is uncomfortable . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What I heard , over and over again , were stories of sorrow , but of shame and anxiety too . Many blamed themselves : Did I do something wrong ? Could I have prevented this ? And , especially : Can I actually do this pregnancy thing ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Taboos that surround women&amp;rsquo ; s bodies , miscarriage shame included , can have severe consequences . Psychologically , physically and emotionally , women shoulder burdens they have little opportunities to unload , except in hushed tones with their closest allies and , in some cases , haphazardly compassionate medical personnel . &lt;p&gt; Ontario needs a more centralized and integrated health-care system as it copes with growing demographic challenges , a premier&amp;rsquo ; s council charged with ending hallway medicine says in its first report . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The initial report from the council headed by retired hospital CEO Dr. Reuben Devlin was released Thursday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It doesn&amp;rsquo ; t contain specific recommendations , but sketches a future of health care in Ontario that likely does not include the current regionalized system of LHINs ( Local Health Integration Networks ) , that is leaner and that is centrally controlled . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;div dir= " ltr " &gt; **28;38325;TOOLONG lang= " en-US " &gt;Here are the findings of the report &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span lang= " en-US " &gt;Hallway Health Care : A system under strain : **35;38355;TOOLONG &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;span lang= " en-US " &gt;&lt;span lang= " en-US " &gt;1,000 patients a day were waiting for a hospital bed on an stretcher or unconventional space in 2018 ; **37;38392;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt; &lt;span lang= " en-US " &gt;&lt;span lang= " en-US " &gt;Visits to emergency departments increased by 11 per cent over the past six years ; **26;38431;TOOLONG &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;Patients who require admission are spending an average of 16 hours in the emergency department before a bed is available ; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;The median wait for long-term care was 146 days in 2017/18 ; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;There has been a 72 per cent increase in emergency department visits and a 79 per cent increase in in-patient admissions for children and youth with mental health issues over past 11 years . &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/div&gt; &lt;/div&gt; &lt;/div&gt; &lt;/div&gt; &lt;/div&gt; &lt;/div&gt; &lt;/div&gt; &lt;/div&gt; &lt;/div&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Ontario&amp;rsquo ; s current health-care system can be characterized as decentralized , large and siloed , and it can be difficult at times to know who is responsible and accountable for ensuring Ontarians have access to high-value health care , &amp;rdquo ; the report says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Stronger lines of accountability would help make the health-care system more efficient and also help ensure Ontario gets a greater value for what it currently spends on health care . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;38459;TOOLONG ... title= " Stethoscopes. " alt= " Stethoscopes. " data-portal-copyright= " Khalil Hamra " **28;38495;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1299279 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The report also notes that there are 21 health-related government agencies supporting the design and delivery of health care in Ontario . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Many of these agencies were created to tackle specific problems , support research , or to establish quality standards and metrics to help the system as it matured . However , these agencies are not always well aligned and there is limited strategic oversight to ensure the efficient and co-ordinated use of resources . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The council is widely expected to kill the regional LHIN system and to replace it with a super agency in charge of everything from Public Health Ontario and the Trillium Gift of Life Network to Cancer Care Ontario . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Critics , including former deputy minister of health Dr. Bob Bell , have warned that such a super agency could decrease the quality of health care in the province . A similar centralization in British Columbia worsened cancer care in the province , Bell said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Ottawa area&amp;rsquo ; s Champlain LHIN gets praise from Bell and others for achievements in co-ordinating and making health care more efficient in the region , but the LHIN system has many critics who call it unnecessarily cumbersome and bureaucratic and who say it was never given the tools to make a real difference . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;38525;TOOLONG ... title= " Emergency room . " alt= " Emergency room . " data-portal-copyright= " Kelly Roche " **28;38561;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1124985 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The interim report spells out many of the well-documented challenges with health care in the province , notably overcrowded hospitals , patients waiting in hospital beds because there is not more suitable care available and the strain on the long-term care system . There are currently 72 long-term care beds per 1,000 people aged 75 or older in the province , a number that is projected to decline to 29 beds per 1,000 people over 75 by 2041 &amp;mdash ; a decline of 60 per cent or the equivalent of 48,000 bed closures &amp;ldquo ; if nothing is done , &amp;rdquo ; says the report . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It acknowledges that Ontario has the lowest per capital spending on health care compared to other provinces and territories , but adds : &amp;ldquo ; The system could work smarter and use this same amount of money to achieve better health outcomes . &amp;rdquo ; Canada , compared to some other countries , spends more but scores lower on some performance indicators. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The solutions to the issues outlined in the report are what worry observers and critics . Although there are bed shortages , simply adding more beds is not the solution , the report says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Bell has been vocal about his concerns that rapid and massive changes could degrade Ontario&amp;rsquo ; s many health care successes , including cancer care . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sudbury MPP France G&amp;eacute ; linas , the NDP health critic , fears the changes will open the door to more privatization of health care across the province , and less input from regions &amp;mdash ; especially northern Ontario . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The province is likely to be divided into five health regions , including one that includes Ottawa and encompasses most of the province east of the GTA . The northern region would include everything north of the French River . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The people who are the most excited about this are the big private healthcare providers , &amp;rdquo ; said G&amp;eacute ; linas. &amp;ldquo ; They will sell a model that is glossy that further opens the door to care based on the ability to pay . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ottawa Hospital CEO Dr. Jack Kitts is among 14 members of the Premier&amp;rsquo ; s Council on Improving Health Care and Ending Hallway Medicine . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;38591;TOOLONG ... launched in support of bus crash survivor after double amputation&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;38626;TOOLONG ... who hear more than one language at home develop attention advantage : study&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;38661;TOOLONG ... Patrick Brazeau : How family -- and a stranger 's kindness -- made life worth living&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; Elizabeth PayneThu , 31 Jan 2019 23:06:29 **45;38696;TOOLONG ... &amp;amp ; ChildLocal NewsMenSeniorsWomenSen . Patrick Brazeau : How family -- and a stranger 's kindness -- made life worth livinghttp : **34;38743;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;38779;TOOLONG ... title= " Senator Patrick Brazeau is shown during a weekend camping trip on the Gatineau River with Ottawa Citizen reporter Gary Dimmock in 2016 . On Bell Let 's Talk Day , Brazeau urges those who need mental health , particularly Indigenous men and boys , support to seek help . " alt= " Senator Patrick Brazeau is shown during a weekend camping trip on the Gatineau River with Ottawa Citizen reporter Gary Dimmock in 2016 . On Bell Let 's Talk Day , Brazeau urges those who need mental health , particularly Indigenous men and boys , support to seek help . " data-portal-copyright= " CHRIS MIKULA " **28;38815;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1342237 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; They say everybody gets a second chance in life . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I must be one of the lucky ones , because I got three . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Three years ago , I was lying on a hospital bed , unconscious , intubated and recovering from serious injuries from a second suicide attempt . It was a time in my life when I had given up on everything and everyone around me. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Today , I am preparing to once again return to work at the Senate . My newborn son , River , brings a smile to my face every day . And I&amp;rsquo ; m building a new life with my soon-to-be-wife , Marie-Claire , who means the world to me. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; My friends and family played a crucial role in my recovery , especially my dad , Marcel , who brought me back to basics and to what really matters in life . But there was one person &amp;mdash ; a stranger &amp;mdash ; who made me realize , at my lowest point , that life is worth living . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As I sat at the end of my bed at the Hull hospital , a surgeon came to see me . I had just woken up from a medically induced coma yet I felt like I was still living a nightmare . I was in complete shock and scared . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But what happened next changed my life . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After asking the standard medical questions , the surgeon lingered . He began to talk to me on a deeper , more human level . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Shaking his head , he asked me what I was doing in that hospital bed . He told me I was lucky to be alive . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I recall him saying , &amp;ldquo ; You&amp;rsquo ; re better than that , &amp;rdquo ; as I lay back in the bed with tears welling up in my eyes . He went on to tell me I had so much more to contribute to the world , and to keep on fighting . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He knew that I am a senator and he even mentioned my previous role as national chief of the Congress of Aboriginal Peoples , but we were still complete strangers . At the end of the conversation , I shook his hand and he suggested I seek treatment after I leave the hospital . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I admitted myself to the psychiatric ward at the Hull hospital for an assessment . Over the following two years , I also saw two psychiatrists who helped me process the events leading up to my near-death. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I uncovered a lot about myself in those sessions . It wasn&amp;rsquo ; t always easy or pleasant to examine my own life so closely but I learned my struggles stemmed from bouts of depression , anxiety and PTSD from turbulent moments in my life that overwhelmed me . For the first time in a long time , I began to feel like I had control over my life again after years of personal and professional turmoil had eaten away at me. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I never saw that surgeon again , but I want him to know how much his words meant to me that day , and that I am OK . Sometimes , all it takes is genuine human connection , even between strangers , to help someone who is in crisis . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One in five Canadians will suffer from a mental illness in their lifetime . I am one of those statistics but I&amp;rsquo ; m still standing today and talking openly about mental health because that&amp;rsquo ; s what saved my life . Stigma is the main reason Canadians who suffer from a mental illness don&amp;rsquo ; t seek help . That&amp;rsquo ; s why events like Bell Let&amp;rsquo ; s Talk are so important because they help break the silence surrounding mental health . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It can be difficult to ask for help . I want men and boys &amp;mdash ; especially Indigenous men and boys &amp;mdash ; to know there is no shame in asking for help when you need it . It&amp;rsquo ; s a lesson I will pass on to my newborn son . Every day that I see him , hold him , hug him and kiss him gives me strength . When I gaze into his loving eyes I know that life is indeed worth living and I feel it in my heart . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **27;38845;TOOLONG . Hospital wants rapid-access mental health clinic among inquest **25;39146;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; Sen. Patrick BrazeauWed , 30 Jan 2019 12:51:36 **45;39173;TOOLONG ... StoryMenWomenConcussion researcher uses high-speed x-ray to look inside pig brains , cadavers and morehttp : **36;39220;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;39258;TOOLONG ... title= " Carleton University professor Oren Petel has developed an x-ray machine capable of taking 100,000 frames per second . " alt= " Carleton University professor Oren Petel has developed an x-ray machine capable of taking 100,000 frames per second . " data-portal-copyright= " Julie Oliver " **28;39294;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1340588 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;39324;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; A Carleton University researcher has invented a high-speed X-ray system that&amp;rsquo ; s now being used to study the effects of collisions on football and hockey helmets , pig brains , synthetic brains and cadavers. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Prof. Oren Petel conducts his research from a small , lead-lined lab on the sixth floor of Carleton&amp;rsquo ; s Canal Building . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The lab is equipped with a linear impactor , a machine&amp;nbsp ; capable of delivering a head hit at 12 metres per second , along with an X-ray system that can capture images of the collision at 100,000 frames per second . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It means Petel and his research team can recreate in spectacular detail what happens to a helmet &amp;mdash ; and to a brain &amp;mdash ; during a high-speed collision . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Instead of looking just at how the head is moving , we can visualize what&amp;rsquo ; s happening to a representative brain model inside the head , &amp;rdquo ; said Petel , a professor in mechanical and aerospace engineering . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The machine&amp;rsquo ; s high-resolution images are used to create a video &amp;mdash ; the process is known as cineradiography &amp;mdash ; that shows the interaction between a helmet and a head while also revealing the brain&amp;rsquo ; s physical response to an impact : how it compresses , twists and stretches . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Taken together , Petel said , the information promises to inform the work of researchers as they design better helmets for hockey and football players , soldiers and cyclists . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s next-level information that can be used to validate the computer models used in helmet design , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;39360;TOOLONG ... title= " Here , he sets up a machine that hits the " head " with great velocity from which he can measure impact and damage to the head . " alt= " Here , he sets up a machine that hits the " head " with great velocity from which he can measure impact and damage to the head . " data-portal-copyright= " Julie Oliver " **28;39396;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1340589 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Petel has submitted patent applications for his test methodology and his imaging system , which is among the fastest in the world . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The system became operational in the summer of 2017 , and is now being deployed in a number of concussion and helmet research projects . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One project , being conducted in partnership with Defence Research and Development Canada , is testing what happens to a synthetic brain inside a plastic head model . Markers are implanted inside the artificial brain to measure how it deforms in a collision . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Another research project , being pursued with Carleton neuroscience professor Matt Holahan , studies how pig brains ( collected from an abattoir ) respond to an impact . &amp;nbsp ; &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; re trying to understand the specific injuries that the cells undergo when the brain stretches , &amp;rdquo ; explained Petel. &amp;ldquo ; We want to know how the stretch and pull response of the brain might lead to injury and , specifically , where those injuries might be occurring . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We want to understand the critical limits of what those cells and those structures can take before they&amp;rsquo ; re affected . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Still another project seeks to validate the computer models now commonly used in head injury research . Those models take information from impact experiments and predict how the brain will respond to the forces involved . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Working with researchers from the University of Ottawa , &amp;nbsp ; Petel&amp;rsquo ; s lab is using cadavers to test the computer models , and to add information about how regions deep in the brain are affected . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The brain is a very complex system and understanding exactly what leads to injury is not a trivial matter . We&amp;rsquo ; re still developing that understanding , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Petel took an unusual path into concussion research . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Born and raised in Montreal , he developed an early interest in physics and decided to study mechanical engineering . At McGill University , he joined the Shockwave Physics Group , where he immersed himself in blast research . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;39426;TOOLONG ... title= " Folds in a human brain . " alt= " Folds in a human brain . " data-portal-copyright= " David Duprey " **28;39462;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1039817 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It just sounded like a lot of fun , things impacting each other , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; And it was really challenging . Your experiments typically last several microseconds , several millionths of a second , and you have to collect all your data in the time before your experiment is destroyed . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As he studied the response of ballistic armour and other protective materials to an explosion , Petel became more and more interested in the dynamics of blast injuries . What was happening internally when a body was hit by a shock wave ? What made the lungs and brain so susceptible to injury ? How was the tissue deforming ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Petel felt that better answers to those questions could improve the design of protective equipment . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He began to study injury biomechanics , and , at one conference , he asked a seasoned researcher why there wasn&amp;rsquo ; t more information about the reaction of internal tissue to a blast . He was told there was no way to measure what happened at such high speeds . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; So why isn&amp;rsquo ; t someone developing something to measure this ? &amp;rdquo ; Petel asked . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The researcher bristled : &amp;ldquo ; If you think you&amp;rsquo ; re so smart , why don&amp;rsquo ; t you do it ? &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A PhD student at the time , Petel took up that challenge . In December 2010 , he launched a private company to attract investment for the development of a high-speed X-ray system . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But commercial investors were unwilling to take a chance on an unproven student , so Petel set his sights on becoming a professor . He figured it was the only way to pursue his idea . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After an exhaustive search , he secured a job in Carleton University&amp;rsquo ; s Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering in August 2013 , and applied for funding to develop his X-ray system and an impact research lab. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Canada Foundation for Innovation and the Ontario Research Fund financed most of the project , which cost about $310,000 and took more than two years to complete . The Canadian Institutes of Health Research and the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council have contributed to the lab&amp;rsquo ; s ongoing research . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Concussion research has come a long way during the past decade , Petel said , but more needs to be done to understand what happens inside the brain during a high-speed collision and how to design a helmet to better protect against injury . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He hopes his research will ultimately make it safer for athletes to compete in sports such as hockey and football . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The ultimate goal of this research is to change the way helmets are designed to improve helmet response , and also to influence in the longer term how helmets are evaluated and the safety standards applied to them . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **27;39492;TOOLONG " **34;39521;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;39557;TOOLONG ... border agent developed appetite for child porn after exposure at work&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;39592;TOOLONG ... remembrance cast against Hitler plan to purge Canadian Jews&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;39627;TOOLONG ... researchers warn that lack of sleep is a public health crisis&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; Andrew DuffyMon , 28 Jan 2019 14:31:26 **45;39662;TOOLONG ... **27;39709;TOOLONG up support : Pain doctor fears treatment options could be restrictedhttp : **30;39738;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;39770;TOOLONG ... title= " Derek Debeer , former drummer with the band Johnny Clegg and Suvuka , who has received treatment from Dr. Ellen Thompson for back and arm pain , which plagues many professional drummers. " alt= " Derek Debeer , former drummer with the band Johnny Clegg and Suvuka , who has received treatment from Dr. Ellen Thompson for back and arm pain , which plagues many professional drummers. " data-portal-copyright= " Errol McGihon " **28;39806;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1340270 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Like many professional drummers , Derek De Beer paid a price for the job he loved . There was a time when the former drummer with the South African band Savuka lived with excruciating back and elbow pain that threatened to end his drumming days . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; De Beer , who has lived in Ottawa for 30 years , searched in vain for help before meeting pain specialist Dr. Ellen Thompson . She injected small amounts of local anaesthetic agents and cortisone into trigger points in the muscles around his painful joints . Attacks every year or two were treated with consistent pain relief . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The treatment worked . It allowed&amp;nbsp ; De Beer to get on with his life and work , which includes teaching drumming and using drumming in his corporate team-building business . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I play drums . I teach a lot and carry a lot . I am pretty hard on my body and it takes a toll , &amp;rdquo ; he says . Still , after having a number of treatments , De Beer has not needed the treatment for five years . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thompson said she has seen good results from the treatment in patients in severe pain and research backs up its effectiveness . But she fears that changes coming in Ontario could limit the ability of doctors to offer the inexpensive and effective treatment . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;39836;TOOLONG ... title= " Derek Debeer " alt= " Derek Debeer " data-portal-copyright= " Errol McGihon " **28;39872;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1340271 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; At a time when steps are being taken to limit opioid prescribing for patients with chronic pain , the injections &amp;ldquo ; represent a major , although limited , period of relief from pain , &amp;rdquo ; Thompson said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Most chronic pain patients state that the degree of relief from local anaesthetic injections is far more profound than the relief provided by even powerful opioids. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thompson said she is worried that such injections will be restricted after concerns were raised by the Ministry of Health about the increased use of nerve blocks and other similar injection procedures in the province between 2009 and 2015 . It has been the subject of discussions between the Ontario Medical Association and the province in ongoing negotiations . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There are reasons why the government may wish to put restrictions on frequency of the injections , Thompson said . Some practitioners are performing a large number of injections on patients per visit . &amp;ldquo ; Having watched some of them in action , it is clear that accuracy and precision is sacrificed to speed and a larger number of injections being performed . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thompson said some practitioners have been billing OHIP hundreds of thousands of dollar a year through performing dozens of injections per visit . There is a fee for each nerve that is injected . The fees for trigger points are less than $20 , she said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There is a need for more sensible methods of paying pain physicians , said Thompson . &amp;ldquo ; But this must be achieved without further jeopardizing pain patients&amp;rsquo ; ability to function . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thompson has previously raised concerns that it has become more difficult to effectively treat chronic pain because of crackdowns on prescribing opioids . The growth in injections could reflect physicians searching for chronic pain relief for their patients without relying on opioids. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Twenty per cent of the population suffers from chronic pain , she noted and treatments that allow sufferers to work , sleep and function are crucial . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thompson said long-lasting chronic pain can often be prevented if the injections are administered in the first few weeks after the onset of pain . For patients with ongoing chronic pain , the treatment can allow them to get some relief to sleep , work and live their lives , she said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Back pain is one of the most expensive problems in all first world countries . No one is treating patients optimally to prevent chronic pain anywhere . We have the skill and knowledge . We need to start using it , even if it will remove a good source of steady income for a large number of clinics and their private investors . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Recent studies have questioned costly spinal fusion surgery that is sometimes offered as a last resort option for back pain patients , finding it is no more effective than non-surgical interventions . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Neil Teitelbaum visited 25 practitioners for help with chronic pain before being treated by Thompson with trigger point injections . Teitelbaum , an electrical and computer engineer , said the treatment left him pain free for three to four years , the most effective relief he has had . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; De Beer , meanwhile , said he recommends the treatment to friends with pain problems and has been tempted to contact well-known drummers , including Phil Collins and Neil Peart of Rush , who are both known to suffer from pain . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; David Jensen , spokesman for the Ministry of Health , said the ministry supports an &amp;ldquo ; evidence-based approach&amp;rdquo ; to managing chronic pain . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Nerve blocks have a role in the management of patients with chronic pain but would rarely be the sole modality of treatment . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Any change to OHIP services or payment formulas , he added , would involve consultations with the Ontario Medical Association and be subject to the current binding arbitration process . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;39902;TOOLONG ... of Ottawa readies test track in Nepean for autonomous vehicle technologies&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;39937;TOOLONG ... assault victim asks court to lift publication ban in her case&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;39972;TOOLONG ... a grip on icy falls in Lanark County&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; Elizabeth PayneFri , 25 Jan 2019 14:21:43 **45;40007;TOOLONG ... &amp;amp ; ChildLocal NewsMenSeniorsWomenIf Ontario scraps its LHINs , what 's next for health care ? http : **35;40054;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;40091;TOOLONG ... title= " A rare site of an empty bed in observation as the emergency department at the Queensway Carleton Hospital .
